games.name: Blot Sweeper
games.tagline: Uncover every clean square without touching an ink blot.
games.meta: Play Blot Sweeper free online: a family-friendly minesweeper with ink blots instead of bombs, drawn on a sketchbook page. Easy, Medium and Hard. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: The classic number-logic puzzle, with ink blots hiding under the paper instead of anything scary. Tap a square to uncover it. Numbers tell you how many blots are touching that square, so you can work out where they are, flag them, and uncover every clean square to win.
facts: Your first tap is always safe
Saves your best on each level
how: Pick a level. Easy is 8×8 with 10 blots, Medium is 9×11 with 18, and Hard is 10×13 with 30.
Tap any square to start. Your first tap is always safe and opens up part of the page.
Each number shows how many ink blots touch that square, including diagonally.
Mark squares you know are blots with a flag: switch to Flag, or press and hold a square.
Uncover every clean square to win. Uncover a blot and the page is ruined.
controls: Tap a square to uncover it.
Switch to 🚩 Flag, press and hold, or right-click to put a flag on a square.
Tap a number when all its blots are flagged to uncover everything around it at once.
The Sound button turns sound on or off.
tips: Start with the 1s next to corners. They often point to exactly one blot.
If a 1 touches only one covered square, that square is a blot. Flag it!
If a number already has all its blots flagged, every other square around it is safe.
Look for the 1-2-1 pattern along an edge: the blots sit under the two 1s.
about: Blot Sweeper is our take on minesweeper, the logic puzzle that came with computers for years. We swapped the bombs for ink blots so it's friendly for younger players.
Every page is random, and your first tap is always safe, so you never lose on a lucky guess.

games.name: Save the Doodle
games.tagline: Guess the word before the eraser rubs out the doodle.
games.meta: Play Save the Doodle free online: a family-friendly hangman word game. Guess letters before the eraser rubs out the pencil doodle. Easy, Medium and Hard word lists with clues.
games.lead: A friendly spin on hangman. A hidden word is shown as blanks with a clue, like Animal or Food. Guess one letter at a time. Every wrong letter makes the eraser rub out part of the little pencil doodle, so fill in the word before it's gone!
facts: Saves your best on each level
Builds a streak of words in a row
how: Pick a level. Easy has short words and 7 tries, Medium has longer words and 6 tries, and Hard has tricky words and 5 tries.
Read the clue, then tap a letter.
If the letter is in the word, it's written in every blank where it belongs.
If it isn't, the eraser rubs out part of the doodle.
Fill in the whole word to save the doodle and add to your streak.
controls: Tap a letter, or type it on a keyboard.
New puzzle gives you a new word.
The Sound button turns sound on or off.
tips: Start with vowels: A, E, I, O and U.
Next try common letters like T, N, S, R and L.
Use the clue! An Animal with three letters and an O in the middle could be DOG or FOX.
Look at the length. Long words often end in -ING or -ER.
about: Save the Doodle is hangman without the hanging. Instead of drawing a scary picture, the eraser rubs out a happy doodle, and your job is to save it.
The word lists are written for kids, grouped into clues like Animal, Food and At school, so younger players have a way in.

games.name: Doodle Doku
games.tagline: Fill the grid so every row, column and box has 1 to 9.
games.meta: Play Doodle Doku free online: sudoku drawn on a sketchbook page. New puzzles every game with exactly one answer, notes, hints and Easy, Medium and Hard levels.
games.lead: Classic sudoku on a pencil grid. Fill every empty square so each row, each column and each 3×3 box has the numbers 1 to 9 exactly once. Every puzzle is new and has exactly one answer, with notes for your pencil guesses and three hints if you get stuck.
facts: Saves your best on each level
how: Pick a level. Easy starts with about 40 numbers, Medium about 32, and Hard as few as 25.
Tap an empty square, then tap a number to write it in.
Each row, column and 3×3 box needs 1 to 9 with no repeats.
A wrong number turns orange and counts as a mistake. Mistakes never end the game.
Fill the whole grid to win. Your best time on each level is saved.
controls: Tap a square, then a number. On a keyboard, use the arrow keys and type 1 to 9.
Notes lets you pencil in small guesses. Erase clears a square.
Hint fills in the square you picked (or a random one), three times per puzzle.
The small number under each button shows how many of that number are still to place.
tips: Look for a row, column or box that's almost full first.
Pick a number and scan for where it can go in each box.
If a square can only take one number, write it in.
Use notes when two squares in a box share the same two possible numbers.
about: Doodle Doku is sudoku with a sketchbook look. Every puzzle is made fresh when you start and checked to have exactly one answer.
We count mistakes but never end the game for them, so it's a good way for kids to learn sudoku at their own pace.

games.name: Crayon Code
games.tagline: Crack the secret row of crayon colours.
games.meta: Play Crayon Code free online: a family-friendly code-breaking puzzle with crayons, like Mastermind. Guess the secret colours using dot clues. Easy, Medium and Hard levels.
games.lead: A code-breaking puzzle with crayons. There's a secret row of colours and you have to work it out. After each guess, dots tell you how close you are: a filled dot for every crayon in the right spot, and an open dot for every right colour in the wrong spot.
facts: Saves your best on each level
how: Pick a level. Easy is 3 colours from 4 crayons. Medium is 4 colours from 6. Hard is 4 colours from 6, and a colour can be used more than once.
Tap crayons to fill your row, then tap Check. Tap a filled spot to clear it.
A filled dot means a crayon is the right colour in the right spot.
An open dot means that colour is in the code, but in a different spot.
The dots don't line up with your crayons, so you have to work out which crayon each dot is about. Crack the code before you run out of rows.
controls: Tap a crayon to add it to the next empty spot.
Tap a spot in your row to clear it, or tap Clear to start the row again.
On a keyboard, press 1 to 6 for crayons, Backspace to undo and Enter to check.
The Sound button turns sound on or off.
tips: Use your first guesses to find out which colours are in the code at all.
If a guess gets no dots, none of those colours are in the code.
Keep one crayon in the same spot and move the others to see which dot changes.
Your fewest guesses on each level is saved. Try to beat it!
about: Crayon Code is our version of the classic code-breaking game, often played with pegs, redrawn with a box of crayons.
It's a great first logic puzzle: Easy is short and simple, and Hard, with repeated colours, will make grown-ups think too.

games.name: Tic-Tac-Doodle
games.tagline: Blue X against pink O. Three in a row wins.
games.meta: Play Tic-Tac-Doodle free online: hand-drawn tic-tac-toe on a sketchbook page. Play a friend on one phone or take on the bot on Easy, Medium or Hard. No downloads, no sign-ups.
games.lead: The classic paper-and-pencil game, drawn right on the sketchbook page. Blue X and pink O take turns, and the first to get three in a row wins the round. Pass the phone to a friend, or try to beat the bot. On Hard it never loses, so a draw is a win!
facts: Play a friend on one device, or the bot
Saves your record against the bot
how: Pick who to play: a friend on the same device, or the bot.
Take turns drawing your mark in an empty square. Blue X is Player 1 (or you), pink O is Player 2 (or the bot).
Get three in a row across, down or corner to corner to win the round.
Fill the board with no line of three and it's a draw. Who goes first swaps every round.
controls: Tap or click a square to draw your mark.
New round starts a fresh board. Mode lets you switch between a friend and the bot.
The Sound button turns sound on or off.
tips: Take the middle square if it's free. It's part of four different lines.
Corners come next: they're part of three lines each.
Always check if the other player has two in a row before you go, and block it.
Make two lines at once (a fork) and the other player can only block one.
about: Tic-Tac-Doodle is tic-tac-toe, the game kids have drawn in the margins of notebooks for generations, redrawn in coloured pencil.
It's a gentle first game against a computer for little ones on Easy, and a real puzzle on Hard, where the bot plays perfectly and the best you can do is a draw.

games.name: Doodle SOS
games.tagline: Write S or O. Spell S-O-S to score and go again.
games.meta: Play Doodle SOS free online: the classic SOS pencil game on a 6x6 grid. Spell S-O-S to score, play a friend on one phone or beat the bot on Easy, Medium or Hard.
games.lead: A pencil-and-paper classic for two. Take turns writing an S or an O in the grid. Finish S-O-S in a line, across, down or corner to corner, and you score a point and go again. When the grid is full, the most SOS lines wins.
facts: Play a friend on one device, or the bot
Saves your record against the bot
how: Pick who to play: a friend on the same device, or the bot.
On your turn, choose S or O with the buttons under the grid, then tap an empty square.
If your letter finishes S-O-S in any direction, it's drawn through in your colour, you score, and you go again.
One letter can finish more than one SOS at once for extra points.
When every square is filled, the player with the most points wins.
controls: Tap S or O to choose your letter, then tap a square to write it.
New round clears the grid. Mode switches between a friend and the bot.
The Sound button turns sound on or off.
tips: Before you write, look for S _ S gaps (write an O) and S O _ gaps (write an S).
Don't leave an S and an O side by side with a gap: that hands the other player a point.
Near the end, count the safe squares left. Sometimes the best move is the one that gives nothing away.
Scoring keeps your turn going, so one good move can set up a chain of points.
about: SOS has been played on scrap paper for a very long time. It looks simple, but it's a game of setting traps and dodging them.
Our version uses a 6×6 sketchbook grid and draws each SOS in the scorer's coloured pencil, so you can see who earned what at a glance.

games.name: Box Doodles
games.tagline: Join the dots. Close a box to claim it and go again.
games.meta: Play Box Doodles free online: the classic dots and boxes game drawn in pencil. Join the dots, claim boxes, and play a friend on one phone or the bot on Easy, Medium or Hard.
games.lead: The dots game from the back of every school notebook. Take turns drawing one line between two dots. Draw the fourth side of a box and it's yours, with your initial in it, and you draw again. When all 25 boxes are claimed, whoever has the most wins.
facts: Play a friend on one device, or the bot
Saves your record against the bot
how: Pick who to play: a friend on the same device, or the bot.
On your turn, tap the space between two dots that sit next to each other to draw a line.
Close the fourth side of a box to claim it. You score a point and draw another line.
When every box has been claimed, the player with the most boxes wins.
controls: Tap or click between two dots to draw a line. On a keyboard, Tab to a line and press Enter.
New round starts a fresh page. Mode switches between a friend and the bot.
The Sound button turns sound on or off.
tips: Avoid drawing the third side of a box. It gives the box away.
Early on, draw lines that don't touch any box with two sides already.
Late in the game every move gives something away. Give away the shortest row of boxes you can.
Taking a box lets you move again, so finish off a chain before you make your next safe move.
about: Dots and boxes has been a favourite pencil game since the 1800s. It starts slow and calm, and ends with long chains of boxes changing hands.
On Hard, the bot takes every box it can and always gives away as little as possible, so you'll have to plan ahead to beat it.

games.name: Paper Boats
games.tagline: Find all four hidden paper boats before they find yours.
games.meta: Play Paper Boats free online: a hide-and-seek boat guessing game on graph paper. Hide your boats, take turns guessing squares, and play a friend on one phone or the bot on Easy, Medium or Hard.
games.lead: A guessing game for two on graph paper. Each player hides four paper boats on their own page. Take turns tapping a square on the other player's page: a miss is a splash, and a hit gets a pencil X. Find every square of a boat and it floats away. Find all four boats first to win.
facts: Play a friend on one device, or the bot
Saves your record against the bot
how: Pick who to play: a friend on the same device, or the bot.
Hide your boats: tap Shuffle until you like where they are, then tap Ready. Boats never touch each other.
Take turns tapping a square on the other player's page. A splash means nothing's there; an X means you hit a boat.
Hit every square of a boat to find it. The first player to find all four boats wins.
Playing a friend? The game asks you to pass the phone between turns, so nobody peeks at the other page.
controls: Tap or click a square on the big page to guess it.
Your own page and boats are shown small underneath, with the other player's guesses on it.
New round hides new boats. Mode switches between a friend and the bot.
The Sound button turns sound on or off.
tips: Spread out your first guesses in a checkerboard pattern. Every boat is at least two squares long, so you'll still find them all.
After a hit, try the squares next to it. After two hits in a line, keep going along that line.
Boats never touch, so the squares all around a found boat are always empty. Don't waste guesses there.
The Boats to find list shows which boats are left. If only the Big boat is left, look for gaps long enough to hold four squares.
about: Paper Boats is our take on the classic grid guessing game, with folded paper boats on a sketchbook page instead of anything scary. Hits are pencil X's and misses are splashes.
The bot gets cleverer with each level: on Easy it mostly guesses, on Medium it hunts around its hits, and on Hard it works out where boats could still be hiding.

games.name: Pencil Parade
games.tagline: Steer a growing parade of little pencil stubs through number gates down a page of lined paper, then climb the book stack for a big bonus.
games.meta: Play Pencil Parade free online. Steer a parade of pencil stubs through the best number gates, dodge bouncy balls and ink puddles, and climb the book stack for a bonus. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: A pencil-sketch runner where your score is a parade of little pencil stubs with smiley faces. Drag left and right to steer the whole parade down a long sheet of lined paper, through gates that add, multiply, subtract or halve your pencils. Dodge rolling bouncy balls, ink puddles, torn holes and spinning compasses along the way. At the end of each level the parade climbs a stack of books, and the higher it gets, the bigger the bonus.
facts: Endless levels that get longer and faster
how: Your parade walks down the page on its own. Drag left or right to steer it, and the whole parade follows.

Gates come in pairs across the path. Blue gates add pencils (+5, +10) or multiply them (×2, ×3). Purple gates take pencils away (−5, −10) or halve the parade (÷2). Your parade goes through whichever side you steer into.
Sometimes both sides are good, so pick the better one. Sometimes both are purple, so pick the one that costs the fewest pencils.
Pencils that bump a bouncy ball, splash into an ink puddle, step in a torn hole or get swept by a spinning compass hop off back to the pencil case, unhurt.
At the book stack the parade climbs books marked ×1 up to ×5, leaving a few pencils behind on each book. Your bonus is the pencils you had at the finish, times the highest book reached, times 10.
Each new level starts with 10 pencils and is longer and faster, with more purple gates and obstacles. If every pencil goes home, the game is over.
controls: Phone or tablet: drag your finger left or right anywhere on the screen. The parade moves with your finger, so you don't need to touch the pencils.
Computer: click and drag left or right with the mouse.
Keyboard: hold the Left and Right arrow keys or A and D to steer. Press P or Escape to pause.
The question mark button shows how to play and pauses the game. The speaker button turns sound on or off.
tips: A ×2 or ×3 gate is worth much more once your parade is big. Early on, a +10 can beat a ×2.
Line up for the next gate early. Big parades are wide, and the whole line needs time to slide across.
Thread small parades through the gaps between puddles and holes. A big parade is safer passing beside an obstacle than through it.
The books cost more pencils on later levels, so save your gains for the book stack.
about: Pencil Parade is a quick sketchbook runner about growing the biggest parade you can. Each choice is a small math puzzle: add or multiply, lose five or lose half. Rolling bouncy balls, ink puddles, torn holes and spinning compasses keep you steering all the way to the book stack.

The book stack finish turns your parade into points. Each book keeps a little tower of pencils behind, and the multiplier on the highest book you reach boosts your bonus. Levels get longer and faster as you go. Nobody gets hurt: pencils that bump into things just hop off to the pencil case for a nap.

games.name: Squiggle Worm
games.tagline: Steer a hand-drawn striped squiggle worm around a page of graph paper, gobble glowing ink dots and grow the longest.
games.meta: Play Squiggle Worm free online. Steer a smiling pencil-doodle worm around a page of graph paper, eat glowing ink dots and ink blots to grow longer, and out-squiggle the other doodles. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: A wiggly arcade game doodled on a page of graph paper. You steer a happy striped squiggle worm across the squares, gobbling glowing ink dots to grow longer and longer. Other coloured-pencil squiggles roam the page too. If one bumps its nose into your body, it goes poof into a puff of pencil scribbles and leaves a trail of ink blots for you to eat. Can you become the longest squiggle on the page?
how: Your worm always squiggles forward. Steer it toward the glowing ink dots to eat them and grow longer.
Your score is your length. The live board in the corner shows the five longest squiggles, and you are in yellow.
If your worm's head bumps into another squiggle's body or the edge of the page, it's bonk and the game is over.
When another squiggle bumps into your body, it goes poof and drops a trail of ink blots. Ink blots are worth extra length!
Hold Zoom to dash. It costs a little length, so use it to grab ink blots or slip past other squiggles. The other squiggles get bigger and bolder the longer you play.
controls: Phone or tablet: drag anywhere to steer, like a joystick. Hold the Zoom button (or a second finger) to dash.
Computer: your worm squiggles toward the mouse pointer. Hold the mouse button to dash.
Keyboard: arrow keys or W A S D to steer, Space to dash.
The sound button turns sound on or off.
tips: Squiggle around the edge of big groups of doodles instead of through them.
Watch the mini-map for the edge of the page and for big squiggles nearby.
Curl around a smaller squiggle so it bumps into you. Then eat its ink blots!
Only dash when you need to. Every dash makes you a little shorter.
about: Squiggle Worm is a grow-the-worm arcade game. You steer a pencil-drawn striped worm across a page of graph paper, eating glowing ink dots to get longer, while other coloured-pencil squiggles roam the same page. If one bumps its nose into your body it goes poof into pencil scribbles and leaves a trail of ink blots; if you bump into theirs, it is game over.

The other squiggles are computer-controlled and get bigger and bolder the longer you survive, so the live leaderboard in the corner is a real race. The Zoom dash costs a little length, which makes every escape a trade. The mini-map is worth a glance before you commit to a turn, especially near the pencil shavings, erasers and paper clips heaped around the page's edge.

games.name: Cookie Drop
games.tagline: Snip the strings and swing a chocolate-chip cookie down to Doodle, the hungry doodle monster.
games.meta: Play Cookie Drop free online. Swipe to snip strings, swing a cookie through the gold stars and drop it to Doodle the doodle monster. 24 pencil-drawn physics puzzles on a corkboard. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: A string-snipping puzzle drawn in pencil on a corkboard. A chocolate-chip cookie hangs from strings tied to thumbtacks, and Doodle the doodle monster is waiting at the bottom with his mouth open. Swipe across a string to snip it and the cookie swings and drops. Time your snips so it lands right in Doodle's mouth, and swing it through the gold stars on the way for up to 3 stars. Bubbles, bouncy balls, paper-clip hooks and puffing party blowers join in as you go.
facts: Saves your stars and best score
how: Swipe across a string to snip it. The cookie swings or drops when its strings let go.
Get the cookie into Doodle's mouth to finish the level. If it plops into the ink puddle, just try again.
Each level has 3 gold stars. Swing the cookie through them for stars and bonus points.
Bubbles float the cookie up until you tap to pop them. Bouncy balls bounce it, paper-clip hooks grab it with a new string, and party blowers puff it along when you tap them.
Your score is your best points from every level added up. Feed Doodle to unlock the next level.
controls: Phone or tablet: swipe across a string to snip it. Tap a bubble or a party blower.
Computer: drag the mouse across a string, or just click it. Click bubbles and party blowers.
Press R to restart the level and L to pick a level.
The Sound button turns sound on or off.
tips: Watch the swing first. Snip when the cookie is heading toward Doodle.
With two or three strings, the order you snip them changes the swing.
A paper-clip hook only grabs the cookie once, so think about where that new swing will go.
Pop a bubble right above Doodle and the cookie drops straight into his mouth.
about: Cookie Drop is a string-snipping physics puzzle sketched in pencil. A chocolate-chip cookie hangs from strings tied to thumbtacks on a corkboard, Doodle the doodle monster waits below with his mouth open, and you swipe to cut strings so the cookie swings and drops into him. Three gold stars on each level reward a clever swing.

The puzzle is in the order and timing of the snips. Bubbles float the cookie up until you pop them, bouncy balls bounce it, paper-clip hooks catch it with a fresh string and party blowers puff it sideways. Nothing is lost by missing; the cookie plops into the ink puddle and you try again.

games.name: Desk Strikes
games.tagline: Swipe a pink eraser down a long wooden ruler and knock over ten smiley pencil stubs.
games.meta: Play Desk Strikes free online. A desk bowling game: swipe to roll a round pink eraser down a ruler lane, curve it into the pocket for strikes, and beat the window draft and a wandering doodle bug over 10 frames with real bowling scoring. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: Ten-pin bowling on a school desk. Swipe up from the eraser to roll it along a long wooden ruler toward ten cheerful pencil stubs with little smiley faces, with a pencil cup and sticky notes doodled behind them. The direction of your swipe aims the eraser, a faster flick rolls it harder, and a bend in your swipe makes it curve. Pencils scatter, tumble into each other and drop off the end of the ruler, and a full 10-frame scoresheet keeps track of every strike and spare. From frame 4 a window draft nudges the eraser, and from frame 7 a friendly doodle bug wanders across the ruler.
facts: Saves your best score and strike streak
how: Swipe up from the eraser to bowl. Where you start the swipe sets the eraser's spot on the ruler, the direction of the swipe aims it, and a faster swipe rolls it harder.
Bend your swipe partway through to curve the eraser. A faint dotted line shows your aim while you drag.
Hit just beside the front pencil, in the pocket, for your best chance at a strike. Each frame gives you two rolls to knock down all ten.
Scoring is real bowling scoring: a strike adds your next two rolls as a bonus and a spare adds your next one. Strikes and spares in frame 10 earn extra rolls, and a perfect game is 300.

Frames 1 to 3 are calm. From frame 4 a window draft pushes the eraser sideways, so check the draft arrow, and from frame 7 a doodle bug scurries across the ruler. Bonk it and your eraser bounces off course, but the bug is fine.
controls: Phone or tablet: put your finger on the eraser and swipe up toward the pencils. Tap during the replay to skip ahead.
Computer: click and drag upward from the eraser, then let go.
Keyboard: Left and Right move the eraser, Up or Space starts the aim sweep, press again to lock it, then Space sets the power on the meter.
The speaker button turns sound on or off.
tips: Aim for the pocket, just beside the front pencil. A dead-center hit often leaves pencils standing on both sides.
A small curve into the pocket knocks more pencils than a perfectly straight roll.
In a draft, aim a little into the wind. More bars on the draft meter means a bigger push.
Watch the doodle bug before you swipe and roll when it has walked out of your path.
about: Desk Strikes is a swipe-to-bowl game on a long wooden ruler laid across a school desk, drawn in pencil on sketchbook paper. You roll a round pink eraser at ten cheerful pencil-stub pins, and the pencils really knock into each other, so a good pocket hit sends them tumbling for a strike. Swipe direction, speed and curve all change the roll.

Each game is a full 10 frames with proper strikes, spares and frame 10 bonus rolls on a classic scoresheet. The game gets trickier as you go, with a window draft from frame 4 and a wandering doodle bug from frame 7. Your best game and your longest strike streak are saved on your device.

games.name: Marble Blitz
games.tagline: Aim, let go, and send a stream of glass marbles bouncing into numbered paper cups before they slide off the desk.
games.meta: Play Marble Blitz free online. Aim your doodle buddy's marbles, bounce them off paper cups to knock their numbers down, grab paper clips for more marbles and keep the cups on the desk. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: A bouncy marble-volley game drawn in pencil on a sheet of notebook paper. Rows of numbered paper cups slide down the page one turn at a time, and your little doodle buddy flicks a whole stream of glass marbles to knock them down. Every bump takes one off a cup's number, and at zero it crumples up. Grab paper clips for more marbles, collect gold star stickers for bonus points, and see how many turns you can last before a cup slides off the edge of the desk.
how: Drag anywhere on the page to aim. The pencil-dotted line shows where your first bounce will land.
Let go and your doodle buddy flicks all its marbles in a quick stream. They bounce off the walls and the paper cups.
Each hit knocks 1 off a cup's number, and a cup crumples when it reaches 0. Paper clips give you an extra marble, gold stars are worth 3 bonus points, and a pink eraser rubs out its whole row.
The first marble to roll back onto the desk sets where your buddy flicks from next. Then every cup slides down one row and a new, tougher row appears at the top.
Your score is the turn you reach plus your bonuses. The game ends when a cup slides off the desk.
controls: Phone or tablet: drag to aim and lift your finger to flick. Tap the page during a volley to speed it up.
Computer: drag with the mouse and release to flick, or use the left and right arrow keys to aim and Space to flick.
During a long volley, Speed up makes the marbles roll faster and Recall marbles brings them all back. New game starts over.
The Sound button turns sound effects on or off.
tips: Bounce your shot off a side wall to get marbles behind a row of cups, where they rattle around and score lots of hits.
Grab the paper clips early. More marbles make every turn stronger.
Clear the cups closest to the desk edge first, especially when they're circled in orange.
Save a pink eraser for a row of big numbers.
about: Marble Blitz is a marble-volley game in the brick-breaker tradition, sketched in graphite on ruled paper. Numbered paper cups slide down one row per turn, and your doodle buddy flicks a stream of glass marbles that bounce off the walls and the cups, knocking one off a number with every hit. When a cup reaches zero it crumples into a puff of paper scraps.

The game is about angles. A shot bounced off a side wall can get your marbles behind a row, where they rattle around and score dozens of hits. Paper clips add marbles, gold stars add points and a pink eraser rubs out a whole row. It ends when a cup slides off the desk, so the cups nearest the edge always come first.

games.name: Paper Peaks
games.tagline: Clear three folded-paper peaks of doodle cards by playing one higher or one lower.
games.meta: Play Paper Peaks free online. A pencil-sketched card puzzle: tap cards one higher or one lower than the notepad card, build long streaks for big points and clear all three paper peaks. Wild doodle stars, hints and undo help on early levels. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: A cheerful card puzzle drawn on a school desk. Three folded-paper mountains are stacked with hand-doodled index cards, and you clear them by tapping any face-up card one higher or one lower than the card on the notepad. Keep a run going for bigger and bigger points, and when nothing fits, flip a new card from the draw pile. Each level hands out fewer wild doodle stars and a shorter draw pile, so plan your runs.
how: Tap any face-up card that is one higher or one lower than the card on the notepad. King and Ace connect, so you can go K, A, 2 or 2, A, K.
Cards flip face up when both cards covering them are gone.
When no card fits, tap the draw pile to flip a new notepad card. The draw pile lights up when it is your only move.
Every card in an unbroken run scores more: 10, 20, 30 and up. Drawing a card ends the run.
Clear all three peaks to win the level. Peak tops are worth 100 bonus points, and every card left in the draw pile is worth 25.
Wild doodle stars in the draw pile, coloured in with every pencil in the box, let any card follow them.
If the draw pile runs out and nothing fits, you lose a pencil and get a fresh deal. Lose all 3 and the game is over.
controls: Tap or click a card to play it, and tap or click the draw pile to draw.
On a keyboard, press 1 to 0 to play a face-up card (numbered left to right), or use the arrow keys and Enter. Space or D draws, U undoes and H shows a hint.
Undo takes back your last move and Hint circles a good card to play. Both are limited each round. The Sound button turns sound on or off.
tips: Before you play, look for the card that keeps your run going longest. Sometimes the lower card opens a longer chain.
Play cards that are covering face-down cards first. Uncovering new cards gives you more choices.
Don't draw while you still have a move. Every card left in the draw pile is worth bonus points at the end.
Save your undo for the end of a round, when one wrong pick can leave you stuck.
about: Paper Peaks is a solitaire card puzzle in the tri-peaks family, dealt across three folded-paper mountains on a sketchbook page. The suits are pencil doodles, stars, hearts, moons and flowers, and you clear cards by tapping any face-up card one higher or one lower than the card on the notepad. King and Ace connect, so a run can wrap all the way around.

The scoring rewards long unbroken runs, and every card left in the draw pile at the end is worth bonus points, so the skill is in not drawing until you have to. Wild doodle stars help, but each level hands out fewer of them and a shorter draw pile. You get three pencils before a game is over.

games.name: Even Sketch
games.tagline: Fill a sheet of graph paper with stars and circles so every row and column balances before the bell rings.
games.meta: Play Even Sketch free online. Fill a sheet of graph paper with stars and circles so every row and column balances, never three in a row, and every = and × sign is obeyed. Endless logic puzzles from 4×4 to 8×8. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: A calm little logic puzzle drawn on a sheet of graph paper. Tap a square to draw a smiling orange star, tap again for a blue circle. Every row and column needs as many stars as circles, you can never have three of the same side by side, and the little = and × badges between squares tell you which pairs match and which are opposite. Each puzzle has exactly one answer, so careful thinking always wins. Finish the page before the bell timer fills up and the next sheet is waiting.
how: Tap a graph-paper square to draw a star, tap it again for a circle, and once more to erase it. Shaded squares with a pencil mark are already filled in and can't be changed.
Every row and every column must have the same number of stars and circles.
Never put more than two of the same doodle next to each other, across or down.
An = badge between two squares means they match. A × badge means one is a star and the other is a circle.
Break a rule and the squares turn pink and wiggle so you can spot it. Fill the whole grid correctly to solve the page.
Each level scores points for solving, 5 points for every second left before the bell and a bonus for not using a hint. If the bell bar fills up first, the game is over.
controls: Phone or tablet: tap a square to cycle star, circle and empty.
Computer: click a square to cycle star, circle and empty.
Keyboard: arrow keys move, Space or Enter cycles, 1 draws a star, 2 a circle and 0 erases. U undoes and H gives a hint.
Undo takes back your last move, Hint reveals one correct square for 10 seconds off the bell timer, and Erase clears the sheet.
The speaker button turns sound on or off.
tips: Look for two of the same side by side. The squares on both ends must be the other doodle.
A gap between two matching doodles, like star, empty, star, has to be a circle.
Once a row has its full half of stars, every empty square left in it is a circle.
Follow the signs: once one square next to an = or × is known, its partner is too.
about: Even Sketch is a balancing logic puzzle. You fill a grid with stars and circles so that each row and column holds the same number of both, no three of a kind ever line up, and every = and × sign between squares is respected. Every puzzle is freshly made and checked to have exactly one solution.

The first levels are small 4×4 sheets with plenty of doodles already pencilled in. Then the grid grows to 6×6, the helpful shaded squares get fewer, more signs appear, and later pages alternate with big 8×8 sheets. A bell timer keeps gentle time pressure on, and your total score carries from page to page until the bell finally rings.

games.name: Doodle Keeper
games.tagline: Guess the hidden word one letter at a time before a bouncing eraser rubs your doodle house off the page.
games.meta: Play Doodle Keeper free online. Guess hidden words letter by letter from a clue, and keep your pencil-drawn doodle house on the page as a cheeky eraser rubs out a piece with every miss. Over 900 family-friendly words. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: A letter-guessing word game drawn in a kid's sketchbook. A clue tells you what kind of word is hidden, like Pencil case, Snacks or Recess fun, and the word sits under a row of paper tiles. Tap the sticky-note keys to guess letters. Right letters flip over with a sparkle, but every wrong letter sends a grinning eraser bouncing across the page to rub out one piece of your doodle house. Solve the word before the doodle is gone to save it, earn a big bonus and move up a level.
how: Read the clue, then guess the hidden word one letter at a time. Every right letter fills in its paper tiles and scores 10 points for each time it appears.
Each wrong letter sends an eraser that rubs out one piece of your doodle house. The doodle starts with 6 pieces, then 5 from level 9 and 4 from level 16.
Solve the word to save the doodle and move up a level. Your bonus is 50 points for every piece still drawn plus 10 points per level.
Solve words with no wrong letters in a row to build a streak. The streak multiplies your bonus, up to three times.
If the doodle is rubbed out, the word is shown and you lose one of your 3 pencils. You carry on at the same level with a new word. When the last pencil is gone, the game is over.
Peek shows one letter for the price of one doodle piece. Every 5 words you solve earns a free Peek.
controls: Phone or tablet: tap the sticky-note keys to guess a letter. Tap Peek to reveal a letter.
Computer: click the sticky-note keys.
Keyboard: type any letter to guess it. Press Enter to start, to get a new word, or to play again.
The speaker button turns sound on or off.
tips: Start with common vowels like E and A, then try S, T, R and N.
Think about the clue. A People at school word often ends in TEACHER, and Action words often end in ING or are short and snappy.
Save Peek for when the doodle still has a few pieces left. It cannot be used on the very last piece unless it is free.
Long words and phrases have more letters to find, so they are often easier than short ones.
about: Doodle Keeper is a classic letter-guessing game drawn in pencil on a sketchbook page. Every hidden word comes with a clue, and there are more than 900 family-friendly answers across 17 categories, from pencil case and classroom things to snacks, pets, recess games, art class and field trips. Words start short and simple, then grow into longer words and phrases like STICKY NOTE and CROSSING GUARD.

Instead of a timer, your doodle house is the countdown. Each wrong guess brings in a cheeky eraser that rubs one piece into a little pile of crumbs, and later levels start with a smaller doodle. Perfect words build a streak that multiplies your bonus, and three pencils give you a few second chances before the page goes blank.

games.name: Letter Scramble
games.tagline: Swipe across a tray of paper letter tiles to find as many words as you can before the timer runs out.
games.meta: Play Letter Scramble free online. Swipe across neighboring paper letter tiles to spell words, hit the target score in 80 seconds, and turn the page to higher levels. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: A fast word search on a desk tray of 16 torn-notebook letter tiles. Swipe from tile to tile, even corner to corner, to spell words of three letters or more. Longer words score much more, and any word that uses the gold-star tile scores double. Reach the target score before the 80-second timer runs out and the next page comes with a bigger target.
how: Swipe across tiles that touch, including diagonals, to spell a word of 3 or more letters. Let go to score it.
Each tile can be used once per word. The bar above the tray turns green for a new word, yellow for a word you already found, and gray if it isn't a word.
Words score 100 points for 3 letters, 300 for 4, 600 for 5, 1,000 for 6, 1,500 for 7 and 2,200 for 8. A word that uses the gold-star tile scores double.
Reach the page's target score before the 80 seconds run out to turn to the next page. Your total score carries over.
Each new page has a higher target. Miss it and it's pencils down.
controls: Phone or tablet: swipe your finger across the tiles, then lift it to score the word. Slide back one tile to undo it.
Computer: click and drag across the tiles, then let go.
Keyboard: type a word to light up its path, press Enter to score it, Backspace to delete a letter and Escape to clear.
The Qu tile counts as two letters, Q and U.
The speaker button turns sound on or off.
tips: Look for endings like S, ED and ING. Adding them to a word you just found is a quick way to score again.
Start your search from the gold-star tile. Even a short word through it is worth double.
Three-letter words add up fast early on, but one long word can be worth ten short ones.
Vowels in the middle of the tray connect to the most neighbors, so build words around them.
about: Letter Scramble is a timed word search on a four-by-four tray of paper letter tiles, each one a little torn notebook square with a pencil letter on it. Swipe across touching tiles, including diagonals, to spell words of three letters or more. Longer words are worth far more than short ones, and any word through the gold-star sticker tile scores double.

Each page gives you 80 seconds to hit a target score, and the target climbs with every page you turn. The word list is family-friendly and checked for real words. It is a quick, repeatable game that rewards vocabulary and a good eye for endings like S, ED and ING.

games.name: Ink Jars
games.tagline: Pour layers of colored ink between glass jars until every jar holds one color.
games.meta: Play Ink Jars free online. Pour layers of colored ink between glass jars on a sketchbook desk until every jar holds just one color. Endless calm levels. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: A calm pouring puzzle on a pencil-sketched desk. Glass ink jars sit on a sheet of paper, each one filled with mixed layers of colored ink. Tap a jar to lift it and tap another to pour. Ink only pours onto the same color or into an empty jar. Fill a jar with one color and it gets a cork with a happy sparkle. Every level is checked by a solver, so it can always be sorted.
facts: Saves your level and best score
how: Tap a jar to lift it, then tap another jar to pour into it.
Ink only pours onto the same color, or into an empty jar. The whole top color pours over, as much as fits.
When a jar is full of one color, it gets a cork. Later levels have taller jars with five layers. Cork every color to finish the level.
Each color has its own little doodle, like a star, heart or moon, so you can tell them apart.
Levels start with 3 colors and grow to 12. Finish in fewer moves for a bigger bonus and three stars.
controls: Phone or tablet: tap a jar to lift it, then tap where to pour.
Computer: click jars, or press 1 to 9 and 0 to pick a jar. The arrow keys and Enter work too.
Undo (or the U key) takes back a pour, 5 times a level. + Jar (or the + key) adds one empty jar per level.
Restart starts the level over. The speaker button turns sound on or off.
tips: Look for jars whose top color matches another jar's top before using an empty jar.
Try to keep one jar empty for as long as you can. It gives you room to sort.
Save + Jar for the big levels with lots of colors.
Beat the par number of moves to earn three stars and the biggest move bonus.
about: Ink Jars is an ink-sorting puzzle. Jars on a sketchbook desk hold mixed layers of colored ink, and you pour from one into another until every jar holds a single color and earns its cork. Ink only pours onto a matching color or into an empty jar, so the empty jar is your most valuable piece.

Every level is checked by a solver before it reaches you, so there is always a way through. Each color has its own little doodle so they are easy to tell apart, and levels grow from three colors to twelve, with taller five-layer jars later on. Beat the par number of moves for three stars.

games.name: Pencil Patrol
games.tagline: Scribble through a notebook-page maze collecting pencil dots while silly erasers chase you.
games.meta: Play Pencil Patrol free online. Guide Stubby the pencil through hand-drawn notebook mazes, collect every pencil dot and dodge four giggly erasers. Grab a gold star sticker to turn the tables and bonk them for big points. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: A maze chase drawn on a notebook page. Stubby the stubby little pencil scribbles through coloured-pencil mazes collecting pencil dots, while four googly-eyed erasers wander around trying to rub him out. Each eraser has its own way of moving, so you can learn to dodge them. Grab a gold star sticker and the erasers go pale and wobbly, and for a few seconds Stubby can bonk them back into the pencil case for bonus points. Clear every dot to turn to the next page, where everything moves a little faster.
facts: 4 pages that repeat and speed up
how: Guide Stubby around the page and collect every pencil dot to clear the level.
Steer before you reach a turn. Stubby remembers your move and takes the next opening that way.
If an eraser touches Stubby, he gets rubbed dizzy and loses a pencil. Lose all 3 pencils and the game is over.
Grab a gold star sticker in a corner and the erasers turn pale for a few seconds. Bonk them for 200, 400, 800 and 1600 points.
Watch for an apple, glue stick or crayon below the pencil case for bonus points. Score 10,000 to earn an extra pencil.
controls: Phone or tablet: swipe anywhere on the page to steer, or use the arrow pad below the maze.
Computer: arrow keys or W, A, S, D to steer. P pauses and M turns sound on or off.
The Pause button stops the game, and the cross button shows or hides the arrow pad.
The sound button turns sound on or off.
tips: Use the side tunnels. Erasers slow down in them, but Stubby doesn't.
Save the gold star until erasers are close, then bonk as many as you can in a row.
Pinky chases you, Smudge tries to get ahead of you, Zigzag zigzags and Dozer gets shy up close.
Every so often the erasers drift back to their own corners, which gives you room to grab dots.
about: Pencil Patrol is a maze-chase game in the spirit of the arcade classics, drawn on a notebook page. Stubby the pencil scribbles through coloured-pencil mazes collecting dots while four googly-eyed erasers try to rub him out, and each eraser has its own habit: Pinky chases, Smudge cuts you off, Zigzag zigzags and Dozer gets shy up close. Learning those habits is the whole game.

The gold star sticker turns the tables for a few seconds, letting Stubby bonk the erasers back into the pencil case for climbing bonus points. Nothing here is scary, just a lot of googly eyes, and every page you clear is a little faster than the last. Stubby, the erasers and the mazes are all our own pencil art.

games.name: Paper Plane Dash
games.tagline: Fly a paper airplane round the inside of a paper tube: dodge the junk, grab the stars, thread the ring gaps. 10 real folds to unlock.
games.meta: Play Paper Plane Dash free online. Touch where you want to fly and your paper airplane loops round the inside of a paper tube drawn on black construction paper, up the sides and over the top, dodging crumpled paper, erasers, pencils, rulers and ink blots, threading the gap in each paper ring, collecting gold stars for Dart Mode and grabbing magnet, shield, boost and x2 power-ups across ten sector pages. Unlock 10 real paper airplane folds, from the Classic Dart to the Delta Wing. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: A fast tube-flying dash drawn in pencil on black construction paper. Your paper airplane flies down a round tube on its own, and you touch or drag on the side of the tube you want to be on: the plane flies round to it the short way, up the sides, over the top and back down, keeping its belly to the wall the whole way. The junk sits on the inside of the tube: crumpled paper balls in every construction-paper colour, erasers, pencil stubs, two-spot-wide rulers and inky blots. Fly round them, fly through the stars, and when a paper ring comes down the tube, get into its gap to fly through for 50 points. Every ten stars start Dart Mode, when your plane fires paper darts that pop everything straight ahead. Catch a magnet to pull stars in, a shield for one free bump, a boost to smash straight through, or a x2 for double points. Every 600 metres turns to a new sector page, each faster than the last, and the stars you collect unlock nine more planes, all real folds: the Basic Glider, Bulldog Dart, Nakamura Lock, Harrier, Hammerhead, Flying Wing, Canard, Stunt Plane and the blue-and-gold Delta Wing.
facts: Touch to fly round the tube
how: Your paper airplane flies down the tube on its own and gets faster with every sector page.
Touch or drag on the side of the tube you want to be on. The plane flies round the inside of the tube to that spot the short way, up the sides, over the top and back, keeping its belly to the wall.

Pick your plane on the start card. The Classic Dart is free, and the stars you collect add up between runs to unlock the Basic Glider, Bulldog Dart, Nakamura Lock, Harrier, Hammerhead, Flying Wing, Canard, Stunt Plane and, last of all, the blue-and-gold Delta Wing.

Dodge crumpled paper, erasers, pencil stubs and paint blobs. Rulers and ink blots are two spots wide. The blue line and the dashed blue arc show your spot; they turn red when something is lined up with you.
Paper rings come down the tube with one gap. Fly round into the gap to pass through for 50 points. Hit the ring and your plane crumples.
Grab gold stars for 10 points each. Every 10 stars fills the meter and starts Dart Mode: for 8 seconds your plane fires paper darts that pop everything straight ahead for 25 points each.
Power-ups: the magnet pulls stars to you, the shield gives you one free bump, the boost smashes through everything (rings too) for 3 seconds, and x2 doubles your points for 10 seconds.
Every 600 metres is a new sector page, with a 100 point bonus. After sector 10, the Ink Vortex, it keeps going faster and faster.
controls: Phone or tablet: touch or drag anywhere on the tube and the plane flies round to that side. Keep your finger down and slide it to steer.
Computer: hold the left or right arrow key (or A and D) to fly round the tube, Up and Down to go to the top or bottom, P or Esc to pause.
Pause stops the action, and the Sound button turns sound effects on or off.
tips: Watch the far end of the tube. Rings show up as a coloured circle long before they arrive, so head for the gap early.
Lines of stars sit in a safe spot, and a ring's stars sit in its gap. Follow them.
The plane always takes the short way round, so a spot straight across the tube is the longest trip. Start moving early.
Dart Mode pops things straight ahead only, so line up with the busiest column while it lasts.
A boost makes you invincible and even smashes rings for 50 points, so spin into the junk on purpose.
Stars count toward new planes even on a short run, so grab every line of them you can.
about: Paper Plane Dash is an original Sketchpad Arcade game, not a twin of anything on our sister site. Your paper airplane flies down the inside of a round tube drawn on black construction paper, and you touch the side of the tube you want to be on. The plane rolls round to it the short way, belly to the wall, dodging crumpled paper balls, erasers, rulers and ink blots.

Every plane you can unlock is a real fold you could make at a desk, from the Basic Glider and Bulldog Dart to the Nakamura Lock, Harrier, Hammerhead and Delta Wing. Stars unlock them, rings and Dart Mode keep a good run exciting, and every 600 metres turns to a faster sector page.

games.name: Margin Merge
games.tagline: Drop smiling doodle balls into a glass jar and merge matching pairs, all the way up to a Super Doodle.
games.meta: Play Margin Merge free online. Drop pencil-drawn doodle balls with dots, stripes, zigzags and swirls into a glass jar, merge matching pairs into bigger, fancier doodles and try to make a Super Doodle. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: A relaxing merge puzzle in a glass jar drawn on notebook paper. Drop doodle balls from the top, and when two of the same kind touch, they merge into the next one up. Climb from a tiny Dot all the way to a big gold Super Doodle, but don't let the jar overflow.
how: Move to aim, then let go to drop a doodle ball into the jar.
When two of the same kind touch, they merge into the next doodle and you score points.
Merges climb from Dot to Stripe, Zigzag, Swirl, Checkers, Sprinkles, Wiggles, Starry, Confetti, Rainbow and Super Doodle.
Two Super Doodles bounce off together for a 100 point bonus.
The game ends when the stack stays above the dotted line at the top of the jar.
controls: Drag or move your mouse to aim, then release or click to drop. On a keyboard, use the arrow keys and Space.
Pop removes one doodle of your choice. You start with one and earn another every 500 points.
New game starts over, and the Sound button turns sound effects on or off.
tips: Keep small doodles together and big ones along the bottom or sides.
Check the Next window before you drop so you can plan where the following piece will go.
A merge can bump into a matching neighbor and set off a combo, so line up chains when you can.
Save your Pop for a small piece stuck between two big ones.
about: Margin Merge is the pencil-sketch twin of one of the most played merge games on our sister site. Two identical pieces that touch combine into the next one up the chain, and the physics are loose and bouncy, so every drop shifts the pile. Here the pieces are smiling doodle balls in a glass jar on a desk, each one fancier than the last, drawn in pencil and coloured pencil.

It is a game about patience more than reflexes. Dropping a small piece next to its match is easy; keeping the big ones from getting buried under the small ones is the skill. Your best score is saved on your device, and the Next window is worth a glance before every drop.

games.name: 2048 DROP
games.title: 2048 DROP – Free Number Merge Game | Sketchpad Arcade
games.tagline: Drop numbers, merge matching balls and work your way to 2048.
games.meta: Play 2048 DROP free online. Drop numbered balls into a pencil-sketched jar on a school desk, combine matching numbers and work your way toward 2048 before the jar fills. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: A number-merging physics puzzle in a pencil-sketched jar on a school desk. Drop numbered balls, watch them roll and settle, and merge matching numbers into bigger ones: 2 and 2 make 4, 4 and 4 make 8, all the way up to 2048 and beyond. Keep the pile below the danger line to stay in the game.
facts: Saves your best and daily scores
how: Move your mouse or drag your finger to slide the waiting ball left and right above the jar.
Click, or let go of the screen, to drop it. Gravity takes over, and the ball rolls and settles on the pile.
When two balls with the same number touch, they merge into one ball worth double. Merges can set off chain reactions.
Every merge scores the value of the new ball, and chain merges earn a bonus. Bigger merges are worth far more.
Keep the pile below the dashed red danger line. If a ball sits above it for about two and a half seconds, the game ends.
controls: Computer: move the mouse to aim and click to drop. Arrow keys aim and Space drops.
Phone and tablet: drag to aim and lift your finger to drop.
NEXT shows the ball you'll drop next, plus a smaller preview of the one after it. The Sound button turns effects on or off.
tips: Keep your biggest numbers together in one corner so they can merge with each other as they grow.
Check NEXT before every drop and leave a spot for it beside a matching number.
Avoid stranding small balls between big ones. A lonely 2 at the bottom can block a whole column.
Keep open space in the middle of the jar so new balls have room to land and roll.
Chain merges score extra, so line up pairs that will set each other off.
A ball crossing the danger line for a moment is fine. Watch the countdown and clear the top before it runs out.
about: 2048 DROP is an original number-merging physics game made by Sketchpad Arcade. It mixes the satisfying doubling of a number puzzle with balls that fall, roll and bounce, so every drop changes the whole pile.

Reaching 2048 is a big moment, but it isn't the end. Skilled players can keep merging to 4096 and beyond. Your personal best, today's best and lifetime stats are saved on your device. No account needed.

games.name: Shoe String Swing
games.tagline: Lasso push-pins with a shoestring and swing a caped kid through the city, the mountains, the farm and beyond.
games.meta: Play Shoe String Swing free online. Hold to lasso the nearest push-pin with a shoestring, swing high and let go to fling a caped superhero kid through the city by day and by flashlight at night, the beach, the snowy mountains and the farm. Grab smiling stars, bounce on bouncy balls and see how far you can go. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: A one-button swinging game starring a caped kid in a mask and a very long shoestring. Hold to lasso the nearest push-pin, swing down and up, then let go to fling forward. Every 1000 meters the scenery changes, from the city to the city at night with a flashlight, then the beach, the snowy mountains and the farm. Catch the next pin before you tumble to the ground, collect stars along the way and see how far you can go.
how: Press and hold to grab the nearest push-pin with your shoestring. The dashed ring shows which pin you'll grab.
Swing down and back up, then let go to fling forward through the air.
Hold again to catch the next pin. If you tumble to the ground, the game is over.
Your score is the distance you swing plus 5 points for every star.
Every 1000 meters you swing into a new place: the city, the city at night (where your flashlight lights the way), the beach, the mountains and the farm.
The farther you go, the farther apart the pins get. Pink balloons bob up and down, and soap bubbles pop soon after you grab them.
controls: Press and hold anywhere on the playfield to grab, and let go to fling. On a keyboard, hold Space or the Up arrow.
Bounce off the bouncy balls for a free boost.
The Sound button turns sound on or off.
tips: Let go just after you pass under the pin and starts to rise. That gives the biggest fling.
Letting go too late sends you straight up. Letting go too early sends you down toward the ground.
Stars follow the swing paths, so a nice smooth swing usually scoops them up.
On a soap bubble, swing once and let go fast before it pops.
about: Shoe String Swing is a one-button swinging game starring a caped kid in a mask with a very long shoestring. Hold to lasso the nearest push-pin, swing under it, and let go at the right moment to fling forward. The scenery changes every 1000 meters, from the city by day to the city at night by flashlight, then the beach, the snowy mountains and the farm.

It is built around rhythm. Once you feel the swing, you can chain pin after pin and scoop up the stars that sit along the swing paths. The hero, the push-pins and all five scenes are our own hand-drawn art, and your best distance is saved on your device.

games.name: Note Quest
games.tagline: Guess the secret word in each note in six tries, with colour clues after every guess.
games.meta: Play Note Quest free online. A secret word is hiding in every folded note. Guess it using green and yellow letter clues, with Beginner, Intermediate and Advanced difficulty. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: A friendly word-guessing game in a sunny classroom. Every note passed your way hides a secret word. Type a guess and the letters light up to show which ones are right. Solve note after note as the words grow from 4 letters to 6, and see how many you can find before you run out of gold stars.
how: Pick Beginner, Intermediate or Advanced, then type a real word and press Enter.
After each guess the letters change colour. Green means the letter is in the right spot. Yellow means it's in the word but in a different spot. Grey means it isn't in the word.
Solve in fewer guesses for more points, and solve notes in a row for a streak bonus.
Miss a word and you lose one of your 3 gold stars. Solve words in a row to win a star back.
Beginner has 4 and 5-letter words, 7 tries and 2 hints. Intermediate grows from 4 to 6 letters with 6 tries and 1 hint. Advanced has 5 and 6-letter words, 5 tries and no hints.
controls: Tap the letters on the on-screen keyboard, or type on your computer keyboard.
Enter checks your guess and the delete key removes a letter.
Hint shows you one letter of the secret word for half points. Beginner gets 2 hints per note, Intermediate 1, Advanced none.
tips: Start with a word that uses lots of different common letters, like a word with A, E and S in it.
Grey keys on the keyboard are letters you can skip.
A yellow letter is in the word, so try it in a new spot on your next guess.
Save your hint for when you're down to your last couple of tries.
about: Note Quest is a word-guessing game in the style of the daily word puzzles many families play together, drawn in pencil. Each note hides a secret word; type a guess and the letters light up to show which are right and in place, right but in the wrong spot, or not in the word at all.

Unlike a once-a-day puzzle, Note Quest keeps going. Words start at four letters and grow to six, and you have a limited supply of tries to spend on wrong guesses. The word list is family-friendly, and all the words are ones you would actually use.

games.name: Eraser Gulp
games.tagline: Steer a hungry little eraser and gulp up the desk to grow.
games.meta: Play Eraser Gulp free online. Steer a cute swirling eraser around a busy school desk, gulp down paper clips, pencils, rulers and even backpacks, and grow big enough to reach the next desk before time runs out. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: A swirly arcade game starring a very hungry little eraser. Glide around a busy school desk and gulp down anything smaller than you. Start with paper clips and gold stars, grow big enough for glue sticks and marbles, then pencil cases, rulers, staplers, desk lamps and backpacks. Fill the size meter before the clock runs out to reach the next, bigger desk.
how: Steer your swirling eraser around the desk.
Glide over things smaller than you to gulp them down. Every gulp makes you a little bigger.
Things that are too big get a red ring when you touch them. Come back when you've grown.
Fill the size meter before the timer runs out to clear the level. Time left over becomes bonus points.
Each new desk is bigger, with a bigger size goal.
controls: On a phone or tablet, drag your finger and the eraser follows it.
With a mouse, move the pointer over the desk and the eraser swirls toward it.
On a keyboard, use the arrow keys or W, A, S and D.
The Sound button turns sound on or off.
tips: Gulp lots of little things at the start. They add up fast.
Pushpin pouches have rulers, tape, pencil cases and glue sticks all close together. Swirl around them for a quick feast.
Big things are worth lots of points, so head for them as soon as they fit.
A banner tells you when a new kind of thing fits, so watch for it.
about: Eraser Gulp is an eat-and-grow arcade game drawn in pencil. You start small enough to gulp the littlest things on the page, and every bite makes you a little bigger, until you can swallow things many times your starting size. Fill the size meter before the clock runs out to move on to a bigger, busier page.

It is silly in the best way. The moment you finally get big enough for the thing that has been in your way all level is the whole point, and younger players in particular seem to love it. The banner that tells you when a new kind of thing fits is worth watching.

games.name: Sidewalk Hop
games.tagline: Hop a kid across busy streets and a creek before the rain catches up.
games.meta: Play Sidewalk Hop free online. Help Milo hop up the neighbourhood, step sideways or back to dodge cars, bikes, scooters and skateboards, ride logs, planks and crates across the creek and stay ahead of the rainstorm. Grab gold stars for bonus points. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: An endless hopping game starring Milo, a curly-haired kid with a red backpack. Hop forward one step at a time, dodge the cars, ice-cream vans and bikes on the streets, and ride logs, planks and crates across the creek. Keep moving, because a rainstorm is chasing you up the street.
how: Hop forward, left, right or back with the arrow buttons under the street. Step sideways or back to dodge traffic and get out of trouble.
Cars, bikes, scooters and skateboards zoom along the streets. Wait for a gap, then hop.
Cross the creek by hopping onto floating logs, planks and crates. Hopping into the water ends the game.
Logs, planks and crates drift along, so hop off before Milo rides off the edge.
A rainstorm creeps up from behind. If it catches up, you are rained out.
You score 1 point for every row forward and 5 points for every gold star.
controls: Tap the arrow buttons under the street to hop forward, left, right or back.
You can also tap the street to hop forward, or swipe in any direction.
On a keyboard, use the arrow keys or W, A, S and D. Space also hops forward.
The Sound button turns sound on or off.
tips: You can hop sideways on a street or a floating log to line up a safer path.
Long logs are the easiest to land on. Little crates need good timing.
Trees, benches, bushes, fire hydrants and trash cans block the way, so plan around them.
Don't wait too long. A few quick hops keep you well ahead of the rain.
about: Sidewalk Hop is an endless hopping game in the tradition of road-crossing arcade games, starring Milo, a curly-haired kid with a red backpack. Hop one step at a time, dodge the cars, ice-cream vans and bikes, ride logs and crates across the creek, and keep moving, because a rainstorm is chasing you up the street.

Every run is different because the streets and creeks are generated as you go, and stars scattered along the way give you a reason to take the risky lane. Milo and his neighbourhood are our own pencil art, and your best distance is saved on your device.

games.name: Paper Gates
games.tagline: Slide patterned blocks out through the gates that match their colour.
games.meta: Play Paper Gates free online. Drag cute patterned blocks around a graph-paper board and slide each one out through the gate of the same colour. Clear every block before time runs out. New boards every level. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: A sliding block puzzle on a sheet of graph paper. The board is packed with cute blocks in bright coloured pencil, each with its own pattern, and the edges have matching gates. Drag each block around the others and slide it into its gate to send it zooming off the page. Clear the whole board before time runs out.
how: Drag a block to slide it. Blocks move around each other but can't overlap.
Slide a block into a gate of the same colour and it leaves the board.
A block only fits through a gate that is at least as wide as the block.
Clear every block before the timer runs out. Time left over becomes bonus points.
Run out of time and you lose a heart and get a new board. Lose all 3 hearts and the game is over.
controls: Press on a block and drag. It slides straight toward your finger, one square at a time, and stops when something is in the way.
Works with a finger on a phone or tablet and with a mouse on a computer.
The Sound button turns sound on or off.
tips: Look for blocks that already have a clear path to their gate and send them out first.
Clearing one block often opens up room for the ones behind it.
Long blocks need wide gates, so check the gate sizes before you start sliding.
Every board can be solved, so if you feel stuck, try moving a different block out of the way.
about: Paper Gates is a sliding-block puzzle on a sheet of graph paper. The board is packed with patterned coloured-pencil blocks, and the edges have matching gates; you drag each block past the others and out through its gate. Clear the whole board before the timer runs out to move on.

Every level is a freshly generated board, so there is nothing to memorise, and the boards grow as you progress. It sits somewhere between a sliding puzzle and a parking puzzle, and it is a good one for players who like to see the whole solution before they touch anything.

games.name: Doodle Stacks
games.tagline: Stack coloured-pencil discs by colour and pop them in tens.
games.meta: Play Doodle Stacks free online. Drag stacks of coloured-pencil discs onto a hexagon board drawn on paper. Stacks with the same top colour hop together, and 10 of a colour pop for points. Chain pops for combos. New colours every level. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: A colour sorting puzzle on a little hexagon board drawn on paper. Three stacks of coloured-pencil discs wait in the wooden tray. Drag one onto an empty spot and any neighbours with the same top colour hop across, one disc at a time. Get 10 or more of one colour on top and they pop in a burst of points. Pop enough discs to finish the level, but don't let the board fill up. Every level adds a new colour, and later ones have rocks in the way.
how: Drag a stack from the tray onto any empty spot on the board.
Stacks next to each other with the same top colour hop together onto one stack.
When 10 or more discs of one colour sit on top of a stack, they pop for points.
One pop can set off another. Chains score combo points.
Pop enough discs to finish the level. If the board fills up, the game is over.
controls: Press on a stack in the tray and drag it onto the board. You can also tap a stack and then tap an empty spot.
Works with a finger on a phone or tablet and with a mouse on a computer.
On a keyboard, press 1, 2 or 3 to pick a stack, move with the arrow keys and press Enter to drop it. W uses the Wipe.
The Wipe button clears one stack off the board, once per level.
The Sound button turns sound on or off.
tips: Keep each colour in its own corner of the board so stacks can grow tall.
Look under the top colour. When it hops away, the colour below might match a neighbour and start a chain.
Save the Wipe for when the board is nearly full.
Don't fill every spot. An empty spot or two gives you room to move.
about: Doodle Stacks is a colour-sorting puzzle on a little hexagon board. You drag a stack of coloured-pencil discs onto an empty space, and any neighbouring stacks with the same colour on top send their discs hopping over one at a time. Build a stack of ten or more of one colour and it pops in a burst of points.

The board is small, so every placement matters, and later levels add new colours and blockers that get in the way. It is a thoughtful game with a satisfying pop at the end of every good chain. Keeping an empty spot or two free is the habit that separates a short game from a long one.

games.name: Scribble Slice
games.tagline: Swipe to slice the juicy fruit that leaps up over the cutting board.
games.meta: Play Scribble Slice free online. Juicy watermelons, pineapples, mangoes and more leap up over a wooden cutting board. Swipe to slice them, chain combos and dodge the inky bombs. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: A juicy slicing game on a big wooden cutting board, drawn in coloured pencil. Watermelons, pineapples, coconuts, mangoes, kiwis and more come leaping up from the bottom of the board. Swipe across them to slice them in half with a big splash of juice. Slice a few in one swipe for a combo bonus, but steer clear of the inky black bombs. The fruit comes faster and in bigger bunches the longer you last.
how: Fruit leaps up from the bottom of the cutting board.
Swipe across a fruit to slice it and score 10 points.
Slice two or more fruit in one swipe for a combo bonus.
Swiping an inky bomb costs a star, and so does letting a fruit fall back down off the board.
Lose all 3 stars and the game is over. Every 500 points gives you a lost star back.
controls: Press and drag your finger across the screen to slice. With a mouse, hold the button down and drag.
Works with a finger on a phone or tablet and with a mouse on a computer.
Press Enter or Space to start a new game.
The Sound button turns sound on or off.
tips: Wait for the fruit to rise to the top of its jump, where it moves slowest, then slice.
Long sweeping swipes through a bunch of fruit score big combos.
Swipe around the inky bombs, not through them. Lift your finger if one is in the way.
A shiny golden apple is worth 50 points, and a bouncy ball slows everything down for a few seconds.
about: Scribble Slice is a fruit-slicing arcade game drawn in pencil. Fruit leaps up into the frame and you swipe across it to cut it in half. Slice several in one stroke for a combo bonus, and steer clear of the inky bombs that come up with it.

Rounds get faster and the fruit comes in bigger bunches the longer you last, so a good run turns into a flurry of swipes. It works especially well on a phone or tablet where you can swipe with a finger, and it is one of the quickest games on the site to pick up.

games.name: Sketch Search
games.tagline: Find the hidden words in a board of graph-paper letter tiles.
games.meta: Play Sketch Search free online. A sketchbook word search with Beginner, Intermediate and Advanced levels and a new theme every round, from pets and toy boxes to bake sales. Drag across the graph-paper letter tiles to find every hidden word before time runs out. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: A cheerful word search on a notebook page. Every level has a theme, like Pets, Art Class or Ice Cream Shop, and a list of words on a sticky note, hidden in a framed board of graph-paper letter tiles. Drag across a word from its first letter to its last and it lights up in a bright colour and gets crossed off your list. Find them all before time runs out. The boards get bigger as you go, and the words start hiding on a slant and even backwards.
how: Pick Beginner, Intermediate or Advanced. Each one keeps its own best score.
Each level has a fun theme and a list of words to find.
Drag in a straight line from the first letter of a word to its last letter.

Beginner words only go across and down, with small boards and plenty of time. Intermediate adds slanted words, then backwards ones. Advanced has big boards with words hiding in every direction from the start, a tighter clock and double points.
Longer words score more, quick finds earn a bonus, and time left over is added at the end of the level.
Run out of time and you lose a star and get a fresh puzzle. Lose all 3 stars and the game is over.
controls: Press on the first letter of a word and drag to the last letter, then let go.
Works with a finger on a phone or tablet and with a mouse on a computer.
Tap Hint (or press H) to flash the first letter of a word you haven't found.
The Sound button turns sound on or off.
tips: Look for unusual letters like K, Y, W or Z first. They are easy to spot and often start a word.
Find the longest words early, while the board is still full of letters to check.
Find words quickly one after another for bonus points.
You get one extra hint for every level you clear, so don't be afraid to use them.
about: Sketch Search is a word search with a theme on every board and a list of words hidden in a grid of letter tiles. Drag from the first letter of a word to the last and it lights up and gets crossed off. Find every word before the timer runs out to move to the next board.

Boards start small with words running left to right and grow into larger grids with words hidden diagonally and backwards. It is a relaxed game that still gives you a reason to hurry, and the themed lists make it a nice one to play with kids who are learning to spell.

games.name: Pencil Putt
games.tagline: Pull back, aim and putt your way round a mini golf course on a school desk.
games.meta: Play Pencil Putt free online. A desktop mini golf game seen from above. Pull back to aim, let go to putt, and sink the ball past pencil shavings, spilled ink, blue arrows, bouncy balls, a wind-up mouse and a spinning coffee mug. 36 holes, then an endless Back Nine Tour. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: A mini golf game on a wooden school desk, seen from above. Each hole is a patch of green on the desktop, with ruler walls, pencil sharpeners and thumbtacks all around. Pull back like a slingshot to aim, let go to putt, and try to sink the ball in as few strokes as you can. Watch out for pencil shavings, spilled ink, pushy blue arrows, bouncy balls, a busy wind-up mouse, a spinning coffee mug and a sliding tape gate. Play all 36 holes, then keep going on the Back Nine Tour, where everything moves faster.
how: Press anywhere on the course and pull back. The dotted line shows where the ball will go.
Pull further for a harder putt, then let go to hit the ball.
Sink the ball in the cup. Beat the par for big points, and a hole in one is worth 1000.
Pencil shavings slow the ball, blue arrows and slopes push it, bouncy balls bounce it and spilled ink costs a stroke.
Finish a hole over par and you lose a star. Lose all 3 stars and the game is over.
controls: Press anywhere, pull back to aim and set the power, then let go to putt.
Works with a finger on a phone or tablet and with a mouse on a computer.
On a keyboard, the left and right arrows aim, up and down set the power and Space putts.
The Sound button turns sound on or off.
tips: A soft putt that stops near the cup is often better than a big whack. A fast ball can roll right over the hole.
Use the walls! A bank shot off the rulers is often the only way round a corner.
Wait for the wind-up mouse and the spinning coffee mug to move out of the way before you putt.
A hole in one wins back a lost star, so it is worth going for it on the short holes.
about: Pencil Putt is a top-down mini golf game with 36 holes on a school desk. Pull back like a slingshot to aim and let go to putt, and try to finish each hole in as few strokes as you can. Ruler walls, pencil sharpeners, shavings and spilled ink make up the basic course, and moving obstacles keep the later holes interesting.

After the full 36, the Back Nine Tour replays the course with everything moving faster. Your best scores per hole are saved on your device, so there is always a stroke or two left to shave off, and a well-judged bank shot off a wall is often the only way round a corner.

games.name: Letter Links
games.tagline: Link words around a chalk path in the park and turn all twelve letters gold. Three difficulties.
games.meta: Play Letter Links free online. Tap chalk letters around a path in the park to make linked words, use all twelve letters in as few words as you can, and beat par. Beginner, Intermediate and Advanced. Works on phone and computer.
games.lead: Twelve chalk letters sit around a path in the park, three on each side. Spell words by hopping from side to side, and each new word starts with the last letter of the one before. Turn every letter gold to solve the puzzle, and do it in par or fewer words for big bonus points. There are 72 puzzles, from easy warm-ups to tricky ones with J, Q and Z. Pick Beginner for easy letters and extra words, Intermediate for the full run, or Advanced for the trickiest puzzles with 4-letter-minimum words and double points.
facts: Saves your best score and progress
how: Tap letters around the path to spell a word. Each next letter must come from a different side.
Press Enter to play the word. Your next word starts with its last letter.
Letters can be used again. Used letters turn gold.
Turn all 12 letters gold to solve the puzzle. Try to do it in the par number of words.
Beginner: easy letters, 7 words per puzzle and 4 hints. Intermediate: all 72 puzzles, 6 words, points ×1.5. Advanced: tricky letters, 4+ letter words only, 5 words, points ×2.
You have 3 heart lives. Running out of words or skipping costs a heart.
